profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 12 sits at 5325 West Capovilla Avenue, Las Vegas, Nevada, on Switch's Core Campus in unincorporated Clark County; this record's own OpenStreetMap tags mark it "landuse=construction," suggesting it may have been mapped mid-build. A separate OSM record in this same dataset, tagged "Switch12," sits nearby but could not be independently confirmed as a distinct Switch facility, since a reverse geocode of that other record's coordinates returned an unrelated business, not a Switch building; this record, Las Vegas 12, is treated as the confirmed building at the 5325 West Capovilla address rather than being merged with that separate, unresolved record. Switch's own current site does not publish individual square footage, megawatt capacity, year-opened, or redundancy-design figures for Las Vegas 12; Switch's official locations page confirms no street addresses for any individual building, directing visitors to a contact form instead, so this address comes from data center industry aggregator directories rather than a direct Switch statement. Switch's Core Campus overall is marketed today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion, growing toward what Switch describes as up to 2.3 million square feet across twelve numbered Las Vegas buildings. Switch's Nevada tax-advantages materials describe a consumer-use-tax abatement to as low as 2 percent and a 75 percent property-tax abatement on customer equipment, administered through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development.

Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs, drawing additional colocation and hyperscale investment from other operators over the past decade. Switch's original 2002 founding purchase, a former Enron-affiliated facility acquired at auction for 930,000 dollars, sat over a fiber-optic backbone corridor that shaped the campus's subsequent growth pattern along South Decatur Boulevard, West Capovilla Avenue, and Lindell Road, the streets along which most of Switch's larger, more recently documented Core Campus buildings, including Las Vegas 8, 9, and 10, are addressed.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 12 is one of twelve buildings planned for Switch's Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, a cluster that the operator describes as reaching 495 megawatts of total power and 2.3 million square feet upon completion. The operator publishes no individual power or space figures for Las Vegas 12 itself. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, a proportional share of 495 megawatts would support roughly 12,000 racks across all twelve buildings, though the actual distribution among buildings is not disclosed.

The Core Campus sits on a fiber corridor established when the operator acquired a former Enron facility at auction in 2002, a location that has anchored subsequent growth across South Decatur Boulevard, West Capovilla Avenue, and Lindell Road in unincorporated Clark County. Switch operates the Core Campus alongside the separate Citadel Campus in Northern Nevada and facilities in Atlanta, Austin, Houston, and Grand Rapids, but Las Vegas remains its largest geographic footprint. Nevada offers a 75 percent property-tax abatement on customer equipment and a consumer-use-tax rate as low as 2 percent.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities, of which only 2 publish megawatt figures, totaling 10.37 megawatts. The Core Campus, with its stated 495 megawatts at completion, would rank as the third-largest published capacity in the state, though this figure is a campus-wide total and Las Vegas 12's individual contribution is not disclosed. An OpenStreetMap tag suggests the facility may have been under construction at the time of that mapping.
